title: When the Witness Breaks Anew
premise: Retired detective Emrys Joubert is paid a suspiciously large retainer by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder scheduled for the spring equinox will never happen — a crime only described in a dead woman's diary. As Emrys investigates, she discovers the 'victim' is the town's beloved matriarch and the diary belongs to a witness officially declared dead five years ago, the same night Emrys closed her last case before retiring in disgrace. The trail forces her to confront the cover-up she helped bury: the witness faked her death to escape the town's most powerful family, who now need her silenced for real before she can testify. In the climax, Emrys finds the living witness hiding in plain sight as the bookshop's reclusive upstairs tenant, and together they turn the would-be murder into a public reckoning at the equinox gathering — justice delivered outside a courtroom that was never going to hold anyone accountable.
about_author: Kestrel Ishikawa is a former court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted ferry cabin on the northern coast, where the fog does half her editing.

chapters.title: Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Emrys Joubert's POV. A pale stranger named Corwin Hale leaves an envelope of cash on the counter of the failing bookshop, asking her to prove a murder won't happen — no name, no date, just a page torn from a diary. Emrys, bored and broke, takes the retainer against her better judgment. Emotional beat: wary curiosity masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. She searches her private case files for anything matching the diary's handwriting and finds it echoes testimony from the Vasseur case she closed five years ago — the one that ended her career. A visit to the old courthouse archive reveals pages missing. Emotional beat: dread resurfacing like a scar reopened.

chapters.title: A Town That Remembers Wrong
chapters.summary: Emrys interviews townsfolk about the anniversary of the Vasseur fire; everyone repeats the same polished story about the witness, Liora Vasseur, dying that night. Only the gravedigger hesitates, saying the coffin weighed nothing. Emotional beat: the first crack in the town's collective lie.

chapters.title: The Diary of a Dead Woman
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. Corwin explains he found the diary while clearing his late aunt's estate; his aunt was the Vasseurs' housekeeper. He confesses he's being followed since reading it. Emrys realizes the diary predicts a future murder, not a past one. Emotional beat: fear becoming complicity.

chapters.title: Equinox, Marked in Red
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The diary's final entry names a victim — Odile Vasseur, the family matriarch — and a date: the spring equinox, six weeks away. Emrys maps the household and its staff, spotting a name redacted so thoroughly it gouged the paper. Emotional beat: cold professional focus hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Tea with the Matriarch
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Under a pretext of appraising Odile's book collection, Emrys visits Vasseur House and meets the sharp-eyed matriarch, who seems to recognize something in Emrys and warns her off with velvet menace. Upstairs, Emrys glimpses a figure behind frosted glass. Emotional beat: predator and predator taking each other's measure.

chapters.title: The Coffin Weighed Nothing
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The gravedigger, bribed with rare first editions, admits he buried an empty box; the death certificate was signed by a doctor since struck off the register. Someone ransacks Emrys's shop overnight but takes only the diary page. Emotional beat: vindication tangled with violation.

chapters.title: What Corwin Didn't Say
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. Corwin is confronted by a man claiming to be a family lawyer demanding the diary; Corwin lies badly and panics. He admits to Emrys that his aunt didn't just keep house — she smuggled letters out of Vasseur House for years. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into terror.

chapters.title: Letters from the Locked Room
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The aunt's hidden correspondence reveals Liora saw something the night of the original crime — not the fire, but what preceded it — and that Odile orchestrated both the cover-up and the fake death to control her own granddaughter. Emotional beat: grief for a girl erased to protect a dynasty.

chapters.title: The Tenant Upstairs
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys reviews her own building's oddities: the quiet tenant, Maren, who pays cash, buys books on ciphering, and never uses the front door after dark. A dropped glove bears monogrammed initials: L.V. Emotional beat: the shock of the answer living above her head all along.

chapters.title: Two Women, One Staircase
chapters.summary: Maren/Liora's POV. Liora narrates her five years of hiding, watching Emrys for signs she'd been sent to finish the job, slowly trusting the retired detective who once failed her. She refuses to testify: last time, the law protected the guilty. Emotional beat: brittle trust offered like a held breath.

chapters.title: The Case That Broke Her
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Flashback woven through present action: how Emrys, fed doctored evidence, declared Liora dead and closed the file, then resigned when doubts wouldn't die. She drafts a confession letter she may never send. Emotional beat: shame finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Odile Summons
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Odile invites Emrys to dinner and offers her a bribe wrapped as respect: retire again, richer, and the past stays past. Emrys declines, and Odile calmly notes that witnesses have died before and will again. Emotional beat: terror met with defiance.

chapters.title: Fire Follows Paper
chapters.summary: Corwin's POV. The aunt's estate burns; Corwin barely escapes with a satchel of documents, injured. He suspects he was meant to die inside. Emrys realizes the equinox murder isn't the plan's beginning — it's the cleanup. Emotional beat: survivor's rage.

chapters.title: The Doctor Who Signed Death
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Tracking the disgraced doctor to a coastal hospice, Emrys gets him to admit Odile paid for the false certificate — and that Odile is dying herself, racing to settle accounts and erase loose ends before her own end. Emotional beat: pity braided with urgency.

chapters.title: A Motive Older Than the Crime
chapters.summary: Liora's POV. Liora finally tells Emrys what she witnessed five years ago: her father's death wasn't accidental, and Odile arranged it to control the inheritance — the same inheritance now motivating a second killing. Emotional beat: catharsis, and the decision to stop running.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. With the trial-equinox deadline looming, Emrys builds a case the police ignored: the empty coffin, the letters, the doctor's statement. The local sheriff, Odile's old friend, warns her to drop it — or be charged with obstruction. Emotional beat: the law revealed as another locked door.

chapters.title: The Trap Baited with Truth
chapters.summary: Liora's POV. Rather than hide until the equinox, Liora proposes they let Odile's fixer come for her — with Emrys waiting. They stage the bookshop as bait, Corwin wired with a recorder, the sheriff reluctantly standing by. Emotional beat: fear converted into strategy.

chapters.title: Night of the Fixer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The attack comes early and wrong; Corwin is taken instead of Liora. Emrys trades the diary's location for Corwin's life, buying hours but losing leverage. Emotional beat: failure's bitter taste, and refusal to stay down.

chapters.title: Equinox
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. At the Vasseur equinox gathering, Emrys and Liora crash the ceremony and expose the plot before the assembled town — playing the recorded confession, producing the doctor, revealing the living witness. Odile's fixer is seized; Odile collapses mid-denial. Emotional beat: the whole town forced to watch what it chose not to see.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The formal system stalls — the sheriff slow-walks charges, lawyers circle — but the town itself turns: the bank calls the Vasseur loans, the church withdraws its blessing, Odile dies within the month, unmourned. Liora testifies eventually, on her own terms. Emotional beat: imperfect, human justice taking root.

chapters.title: Shelved Under L
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Weeks later, the bookshop has customers again; Corwin works the register, Liora alphabetizes the mystery section under her real name. Emrys files her confession letter in a drawer marked 'someday' and, for the first time in five years, sleeps soundly. Emotional beat: belonging earned, quiet and durable.
